answer: Humans: healthy adults (first-in-human, 43 plus 12 randomised, ages up to 56) and adults with treatment-resistant depression (72 randomised, 70 treated, ages 18-65); endpoints were safety, PK, resting EEG and QTcF (healthy) and MADRS at 24 h with 48 h and week 6 (TRD); commonest events dizziness, transient amnesia, somnolence, mild dissociative events; positive exposure-QTcF relation in healthy volunteers; a ketamine reference arm in the Spanish sites; sponsor-authored. No non-psychiatric context found in the registry or literature perimeter. This is exposure and activity in another disease, not utility or safety in WOREE.
label: DATO (what the papers state) / IPOTESI (any bearing on WOREE: none supported)
what_is_not_known: Supplementary appendices of the phase 2 paper; any exposure in epilepsy, developmental disease, older or younger age; the unshown PET occupancy ('data on file'); why one sponsor study was terminated (only 'terminated by the sponsor' read).

answer: Potency depends on pH for this compound by declaration (about 6-fold more potent at pH 6.9 than 7.6) and a 2017 abstract by the same group gives IC50 21 nM at pH 6.9 and 130 nM at pH 7.6 (6.2-fold, human GluN2B in oocytes, no conditions); the registry 7.64 (23 nM, pH 6.9) is the same measurement as the 21 nM reported again, not a second one. The maximum effect at either pH and the recording conditions are not in any file for NP10679. For the series prototype (93-31, not NP10679) potency shifted about 9.5-fold between pH 7.6 and 6.9 while the fitted maximum stayed 76 to 83 percent. Molecule or class: both, graded. The size is a property of the molecule (side-chain isomers 9.4 versus 2.9-fold), the pH-sensing site belongs to the ifenprodil-site region, and older abstracts say ifenprodil and CP-101,606 are also proton-sensitive, yet the 2015 paper declares those antagonists lack substantial pH sensitivity (supplement not reached).
label: DATO (series measured; NP10679 declared) / INFERENZA (that NP10679's maximum behaves like the prototype's)
what_is_not_known: NP10679's maximum effect and recording conditions at each pH (the IC50 pair exists at abstract level); ifenprodil's measured pH shift (Table S6 not reached); the discovery paper 34493631 behind the registry value was not opened.

answer: Site: not tested for NP10679 in any source reached; the series prototype was docked at the ifenprodil-site interface and its pH ratio was lowered by GluN1 Gly112 and GluN2B residue 106, 206 or 235 mutations (ratios 2.6, 1.0, 1.5 against 9.5; the Glu106:Glu235 sensor is a candidate, INFERENZA); NP10679 is an aryl-piperazine propanolamine like the earlier NP10075 (docked similarly), so its ifenprodil-site action is inferred. GluN2B selectivity: more than 100,000-fold declared, no data in the paper read. Off-target: H1 73 and 40 nM and hERG 620 and 621 nM are same-origin repeats from two developer reports, and the 30-fold hERG margin has an unstated pH (about 5-fold against the pH 7.6 potency, INFERENZA). Species and assembly: registry row human GluN2B in oocytes; series work rat GluN1/GluN2B oocytes with a triheteromer gain of 4.4-fold for the prototype only. Mg2+, voltage and use dependence: not in any source reached (oocyte recordings were Mg2+-free at -40 mV).
label: DATO (series) / INFERENZA (NP10679 site) / DATO (absence for Mg2+, voltage, use, triheteromer)
what_is_not_known: Direct competition or mutagenesis for NP10679; maximum effect on triheteromers; Mg2+, voltage and use dependence; whether the pH sensor residues act the same for NP10679; the selectivity assays.

answer: Human data: two phase 1 studies in healthy adults (48 and 24; ages 18-55): atypical somnolence with ready arousal (dose dependence stated for the single-administration study; in the repeated-administration study three placebo subjects also had it), no dissociative or cognitive-test signal, no serious events, no ECG signal in the first study; developer-authored; ClinicalTrials.gov lists only these two phase 1 studies. It does not say anything about efficacy, patients, tissue acidity, epilepsy or children. H1 antagonism (declared 73 nM) is a sedation confound for behavioural or EEG readouts.
label: DATO (what the paper states) / IPOTESI (any bearing on WOREE: none supported)
what_is_not_known: Any phase 2 result (a subarachnoid-haemorrhage programme is described in the 2025 abstract; nothing registered under these strings); human CSF or brain exposure; effect of acid pH on human safety margins.
